drivingQuestion: Does the mishna imply unflawed young women receive no fine?
outcomeNote: resolved by rereading the mishna's scope

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ הָנֵי נְעָרוֹת, פְּסוּלוֹת אִית לְהוּ קְנָס, כְּשֵׁירוֹת לָא?! הָכִי קָאָמַר: אֵלּוּ נְעָרוֹת פְּסוּלוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם קְנָס — הַבָּא עַל הַמַּמְזֶרֶת וְעַל הַנְּתִינָה וְעַל הַכּוּתִית.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara wonders: Is it «these young women» with «flawed» lineage listed in the mishna, «for whom there is a fine» paid if they are raped, while for young women with «unflawed» lineage, «no,» there is no fine? The Gemara explains that «this» is what the tanna «is saying: These are» the «young women» with «flawed» lineage «for whom there is a fine» paid if they are raped. This is not a comprehensive list; rather, the tanna enumerates those young women for whom a fine is paid despite their flawed lineage: «One who has relations with a mamzeret, or with a Gibeonite woman, or with a Samaritan woman.»
